title: Design an Elevator System
summary: Run a bank of elevators where each car follows the LOOK algorithm — sweep one way serving every stop, reverse only when nothing is ahead — and the choice of which car answers a hall call is a strategy that can be tuned without any car noticing.
concepts: The LOOK/SCAN algorithm, and why nearest-first starves riders
Serving a stop only in the direction the rider wants to travel
Hall calls and car calls as genuinely different request types
Separating which car is chosen from how a car behaves once chosen
Tick-based simulation so scheduling is testable without threads
Wall-clock time versus total distance as competing objectives
extensions: Run each elevator on its own thread with a real controller
Add weight-based capacity so a full car skips hall calls
Add express elevators that serve only some floors
Add emergency and fire-service modes that override scheduling
Add destination dispatch, where riders enter their floor in the lobby
Handle a car that fails mid-journey and reassign its riders
